title: Desktop: a ChatGPT Codex sign-in finishes without pasting, whichever way the page opens it
steps: S1: run the tracy-desktop subscription-handoff tests (node:test; a real loopback server on a free port, fake browser and fake window).

S2: the end-to-end form: in the desktop app, Getting started or Settings > AI accounts > ChatGPT Codex > Connect; finish OpenAI sign-in in the browser; the tab says 'Signed in. You can close this tab and return to Tracy Cowork.' and the app shows the account connected without a paste.
expect: The page asking the app to open the Codex authorize address (tracyDesktop.links.openExternal) starts the catcher, then opens the browser.
A callback with the attempt's path and state gets a 200 HTML page, is delivered once as tracy-subscription-callback, and the catcher stops.

A wrong state or another path gets a 404 and the catcher keeps listening; a busy port logs one line and leaves the paste path; the catcher stops after its time runs out; a second attempt replaces the first.
The delivery script carries the URL as JSON data, whatever characters it holds.

tests: a Codex callback with the expected state is answered, delivered once, and the catcher stops
a wrong state or another path gets a plain 404 and the catcher keeps listening
the catcher stops by itself when the attempt runs out of time
a busy port logs one line, still opens the browser, and never delivers
a second attempt replaces the first
the Codex authorize address names the callback path and state to catch
the page asking the app to open a Codex sign-in starts the catcher, then the browser
any other address the page opens goes to the browser with no catcher
the delivery script dispatches the callback event with the URL as data, whatever it holds

fence: the catcher listens only for a known vendor's authorize address opened from a page on the window's own origin, and delivers only to that origin
